title: Cold-Bridge Warmup Coordinator: progressive weight streaming + KV conditioning for low-latency dedicated capacity
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem statement: Customers on Redwood Dedicated experience occasional 200-800ms cold-start token latency spikes during first requests after scale-up or node replacement. These spikes erode P50/P95 SLOs for throughput-guaranteed reservations and complicate autoscaler decisions during bursty traffic.

Proposal summary: Build a coordinated Cold-Bridge Warmup Coordinator (CBWC) that orchestrates two complementary processes when a dedicated node/fleet slot is claimed or enters active duty: 1) progressive weight streaming (slab-by-slab) optimized for request-critical layers, and 2) KV-conditioning: a lightweight, access-pattern-driven KV priming pass that populates prefix caches and short-lived KV heuristics. CBWC will be admission-controller aware and tie into autoscaling policies so that capacity transitions carry a warmness score used by routing and SLA accounting.

Key design ideas and differentiators (compared to past approaches):
- Two-phase warm strategy: prioritize minimal critical-path model shards first (embedding/attention layers) to allow early inference with degraded but correct outputs while background layer streaming continues. This reduces worst-case first-token latency compared to naive full-weight streaming.
- KV-conditioning as heuristic passes (not full materialization): instead of precomputing full KV snapshots, CBWC runs short, targeted synthetic probes derived from recent tenant traces (anonymized) to seed common key prefixes and synthesize high-hit hotlists. This is cheaper than full population and more effective than random seeding.
- Warmness score: a numeric vector (0-100) tracked per node and per tenant allocation that captures: percent weight residency for critical slabs, KV-hit-probability estimate, and recent verified inference latency. This drives routing/weighting logic so that customer requests can be routed preferentially to nodes with higher warmness when possible.
- Autoscaler integration: CBWC exposes a warmness-aware admission policy. Autoscaler can choose between (A) optimistic scale-up with CBWC warmup and graded routing, or (B) conservative scale-up (reserve-only) for strict throughput-guarantee customers. Policy choice is per-dedicated-bundle and configurable in the Dedicated UI/API.

Trade-offs considered:
- Cost vs latency: Progressive streaming reduces latency but increases temporary network IO. We will cap background streaming bandwidth and expose a cost-lever to customers (background-bandwidth-limit).
- Security/anonymization: KV-conditioning uses trace-derived probes. We will only use aggregated n-gram frequency lists and stop using any identifiable customer prompt content. All probe generation happens within tenant scope or via anonymized pool.
- Complexity vs benefit: Warmness score adds routing complexity; we will begin with a single scalar warmness and validate before adding multi-dimensional routing heuristics.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Spec and simulation (2 weeks): build a simulator that replays production traffic traces against a virtual CBWC to measure P50/P95 improvement and network/cost overhead.
2) Lightweight prototype (3 weeks): server-side CBWC daemon that exposes warmness and performs slab-priority streaming + synthetic KV-probing using anonymized trace artifacts. Feature-gated behind a runtime flag.
3) Integration with autoscaler and routing (2 weeks): warmness API, admission hooks, routing weight adjustments.
4) Canary and telemetry (3 weeks): roll out to internal dedicated fleets, measure metrics, iterate.
5) Customer beta (ongoing): enable for selected tenants with throughput guarantees.

Operational considerations:
- Metrics to track: first-token latency, P50/P95 token latency, warmness distribution, background network IO per-node, KV-hit-rate pre/post-conditioning, cost delta per-tenancy.
- Alerts: warmup-failure-rate > 1% for 1h, warmness not improving after 90s post-claim, background bandwidth exceeding configured cap.
- Rollback plan: CBWC disabled at fleet-level via feature flag; nodes gracefully accept traffic but will not perform streaming or probes.

- Simulation notebook (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/infra/CBWC+Simulation
- Design doc (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/infra/Cold-Bridge+Warmup+Coordinator+Design
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/4567
- Routing integration PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/1228
- Eviction policy dependency: see ENG-110234

Open questions:
- What is the minimum critical slab set that guarantees usable early outputs for large models? (Action: schedule microbenchmarks across model family variants)
- How to safely generate anonymized KV probes for highly specialized tenant vocabularies?
- Acceptable background bandwidth caps for Dedicated Small/Medium/Large SKUs?
acceptance_criteria: Simulator shows >= 40% reduction in first-request P95 for scaled-up nodes under bursty workload profiles with <10% background bandwidth overhead
Prototype exposes a warmness scalar via runtime API and routing honors warmness weights in canary canary-enabled-release
KV-conditioning process runs with no PII leakage (privacy checklist signed) and material cost < $X/month per-tenant (TBD)
Autoscaler policy knob (optimistic vs conservative) present in Dedicated API and tested in unit/integration tests
Telemetry dashboards for warmness, KV-hit-rate, and stream bandwidth created in Grafana and surfaced in Console
Canary on internal fleets for 2 weeks with defined rollback criteria passed
notes: 2025-01-16: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, Routing, and Dedicated PMs. Agreed to start with simulator. Attendees: Diego, Ava, Priya (PM), Lars (Routing lead).
2025-01-22: Simulator skeleton complete. Early runs show 20-30% median improvement on small traces. Need larger trace set.

2025-01-29: Privacy review requested for KV probe approach. Security noted requirement to only use aggregated token-frequency lists and to keep probe generation inside tenant VPC for Private customers.
2025-02-03: Prototype initial commit (see PR #4567). Implements slab-priority driver and a synthetic-probe generator using top-100 n-grams per-tenant.
2025-02-07: Routing team prototyped warmness-aware weight adjustment; routing change is feature-flagged. Early internal routing tests look stable.

2025-02-10: Meeting with Sales/Customer Success to propose opt-in beta for three enterprise customers with strict throughput guarantees; they requested billing transparency for background streaming costs.
2025-02-12: Updated spec to include background-bandwidth-limit and warmness scalar (0-100). Marking In Progress and starting integration sprint.
